terms.gloss: the supine, the verbal noun in -um and -ū
evidence: Charis. p. 153 P.; Prisc. p. 811 P. (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The later grammarians’ name. Quintilian has no single word for it and calls these forms verba participiālia (1.4.29): dictū, factū.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 249.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
